questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
(i) An interrupt that can be temporarily ignored by the system is known as Maskable interrupt.
(ii) Horizontal microprogramming uses one bit for each control signal.
(iii) Computer organization deals with structural relationships that are not visible to the
programmer whereas computer architecture deals with the functional behaviour of a computer system as viewed by programmer.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(d)
• A maskable interrupt can be temporarily disabled by setting a specific bit in a control register.
• In horizontal microprogramming, each bit is identified specifically with a single control point, which indicates the corresponding micro-operation to be executed.
• Computer architecture is focused on the design of the internal workings of a computer system, while computer organization is focused on the implementation of that design.
All the statements are correct. Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
(i) In case of pipeline processor, loop buffer is very high speed memory maintained by instruction fetch.
(ii) The process of fetching and executing instructions one at a time, in the order of increasing addresses is known as straight line sequencing.
(iii) In RISC instruction set, all arithmetic/logic instructions must be register based.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• A loop buffer is a small, very-high-speed memory maintained by the instruction fetch stage of the pipeline and containing the ‘n’ most recently fetched instructions, in sequence. The instructions fetched in sequence will be available without the usual memory access time well suited to dealing with loops.
• In straight line sequencing, the instruction of a program is executed in a sequential manner (i.e. every time PC is incremented by a fixed offset).
• RISC architectures rely on registers for operand storage and manipulation, reducing memory access overhead. Therefore, the arithmetic/logic instructions are register based.
Hence, all the above statements are correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement(s) is/are true with regard to instruction pipelining?

options.text: The basic goal of instruction pipelining is to achieve a CPI of 1.
Instruction set architecture having simple register addressing modes can be easily pipelined than those having complex addressing modes.
By the use of hardware special features and compiler design techniques, pipeline hazards can be removed.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
The primary goal of instruction pipelining is to achieve a CPI of 1 but not more than 1 so that one instruction is completed per clock cycle. Hence, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext: The following diagram shows, which addressing mode for 6802 MPU?
questions.solution:
(c)
For 6802 MPU, in direct addressing, the address of the operand is contained in the second byte of the instruction. Direct addressing allows the user to directly address the lowest 256 bytes of the memory, i.e, locations 0 through 255. Enhanced execution times are achieved by storing data in these locations. In extended addressing mode, the address contained in the second byte of the instruction is used as the higher eight bits of the address of the operand. The third byte of the instruction is used as the lower eight bits of the address for the operand. Thus, the given diagram represents extended addressing mode.

questions.qtext: Given below are some statements associated with the registers of a CPU. Identify the true statements(s):

options.text: The program counter holds the memory address of the instruction in execution.
Only opcode is transferred to the control unit.
An instruction in the instruction register consists of the opcode and the operand.
The value of the program counter is incremented by 1 once its value has been read to the memory address register.

questions.solution:
(b, c, d)
• Program counter contain the address of next instruction to be fetched but not address of executed instruction. Hence, option (a) is incorrect.
• The instruction in the instruction register, includes the opcode and operand. The control unit decodes the instruction based on the opcode. Hence, only opcode is transferred to the control unit.
• After the CPU fetches the instruction, it increases the program counter by 1 to point to the next instruction in the program's sequence.
Hence, options (b), (c) and (d) are correct.
